== Tournament director cross-reference ==

=== Possibly faulty data ===
* [[Jeff Weitkamp]] is described in the source as "Tournament Director Jeff Weitkamp - Gold 40" of the Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck tournament only (Francis K. Lalumiere, 5 October 2000). His page says exactly that. The lead of this page says Justin Pakes directed the Star Wars rooms, so he was not the director of the whole convention.
* The Gold 40 slot matches the [[Squadron Members]] listing for Jeff Weitkamp, which is how the two were identified as the same person.

=== Build notes ===
* Source: Wayback capture of decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/reports/fkl2.html (7 January 2001). The page already cited it as ref "fkl2".

== Style pass (2026-10-15) ==
=== Possibly faulty data ===
* Day 1 attendance: Wikipedia and ''Star Wars Insider'' 52 give 72 Day 1 players; Francis K. Lalumiere ("Mighty Jabba Sails Across the Atlantic", Decipher, 5 October 2000) put 170 competitors in the main hall fighting for a Day 2 seat. Article now states 72 and cites all three.
=== Marginal cuts ===
* Removed (uncited): "Decipher had announced its ''The Lord of the Rings'' Trading Card Game licence on 10 August 2000. A LOTR TCG poster hung behind Baksa's signing table in the official photographs." Caption also said "with a ''Lord of the Rings'' TCG poster behind the table".
* Removed: "Brian posted both photographs on 14 November 2020; the overlay on the celebration frame reads 'Team Albany / 2000 Star Wars CCG Team Champs.'" (source: Brian Terwilliger, X, 14 November 2020).
* Team photo caption order was given as "Left to right: Chris Terwilliger, Matt Sokol, Brian Terwilliger, Jonny Chu"; names are kept in that order.
* Photo gallery mechanics cut: Decipher's gallery was JavaScript (<code>/deciphercon/2000/photos/</code>); thumbnail clicks opened pop-ups and crawlers mostly missed the full JPEGs; the eleven 400×300 originals were recovered from <code>http://decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/photos/pictures/{id}.jpg</code>.
* Card-toss anecdote source: Charles Hickey, "mr-hickey-goes-to-florida", Decktech (14 October 2000).
* Hallway caption detail cut: one still shows a player wearing a DecipherCon 2000 shirt; another Kevin Reitzel waving at the camera.
* Removed "Preserved copy" body bullets in the video sections; the copies remain in the refs and Sources.

== Convention hub split (2026-10-17) ==
=== Build notes ===
* [[2000 Decipher World Championship]] is now the subarticle for Day 1–3, the Final Confrontation, the FC video, and the championship-match interview. This page keeps venue, guests, seminars, side events, the Sunday team event, other games, trip-report operations, and photographs.
* Lead thumbs are hallway 5 (Doubletree lobby interior) and the guests-signing still. Worlds keeps the hall and champion plaque. No contemporaneous licensed facade of 3011 Maingate Lane was found (Commons, Flickr CC, historic postcard, Decipher gallery). The same building later operated as Holiday Inn Resort Kissimmee by the Parks (Travel Weekly; telephone still 407-396-1400). Seralago (5678 W Irlo Bronson) is a different hotel. DoubleTree Universal and DoubleTree SeaWorld are different hotels.
* Street address 3011 Maingate Lane also appears on a 8 October 2000 post from a guest at the same Doubletree (corfid.com/vbb/showthread.php?p=135872). Body cites Travel Weekly for the standing building.
* Hallway gallery cut to three group stills: Reitzel four-player (3), Colson (4), Colson in the lobby (5). Dropped hallway 1–2 (Reitzel close-ups) and File:Jim Colson DecipherCon 2000.jpg from this page. Dropped Young Jedi staff, STCCG plaque, Young Jedi uncut sheets, and Great Tribble Hunt banner (other-game-only; SWCCG-first).
=== Possibly faulty data ===
* Day 1 start: Sokol contemporaneous ~1 p.m., three hours after posted time (schedule 10 a.m.). Arendt waited three hours. Hayes PDS2 46:34–46:54: poorly run; first round paired at 1 p.m. when it was supposed to start at 8 or 9 a.m.; done at 2 a.m.; "five hours late." Body uses 1 p.m. (Sokol + Hayes pairings) and the 2 a.m. finish (Hayes).
* Tournament software: Bill recalled [[Matt Sokol]] PDS2 saying software broke and pairings were done by hand. Sokol auto-captions and a whisper of 38:00–46:00 do not have that claim. [[Paul Todd Feldman]] PDS2 40:28–40:37 (whisper-checked): "people said like the software was not working properly" / "I know it took forever." Body dests Feldman, not Sokol, and does not dest "by hand."
* Card flipping: Bill recalled Hayes PDS2 on people flipping cards. Hayes "as soon as he flips" at ~49:02 is a Star Trek Visage / Ray Bour / first-Gen-Con story, not 2000 Star Wars. Closest sourced 2000 claim is scouting (Hayes 50:43–51:12): players walked behind tables and shared what opponents played. That sentence is on the Worlds Recollections section.
* TFN preview (5 September 2000) said "over 75 tournaments." Decipher home/schedule: more than 60. Body follows Decipher.
=== Marginal cuts ===
* Final Confrontation Game 1/2 prose, FC video still/links, and Championship Match Interview moved to [[2000 Decipher World Championship]] (already there at live 105555).
* Team Albany overnight ISB build stays on Worlds.
* YJ/ST/JK/LOTR seminar grid (Chuck Design-A-Card, Ellington/Martinson, Dean Irwin, LOTR reverse Q&A) left as other-game brief; SWCCG Q&A (Lischke) and card-production / Digital Deck kept.
* Loftus: ~dozen women in YJ Day 2; Roxanne Barbour only woman in ST Worlds; no woman in SW Worlds fifth year. Cut (other-game / one-line aside).
